item.title: Israeli forces board Gaza-bound flotilla near Cyprus, activists say
item.description: Live broadcasts from the Global Sumud flotilla show commandos boarding several boats trying to breach the Gaza maritime blockade.

item.title: Prince William selling 20% of duchy property for housing and nature projects
item.description: The Duchy of Cornwall is to sell part of its 128,000 acre estate and re-invest in more housing.

item.title: Shakira wins £50m tax refund from Spanish government
item.description: The Colombian singer says the court ruling means the "narrative" that she was guilty now "crumbles".

item.title: Bodies of missing Italian divers found in Maldives
item.description: The bodies of all five Italian divers who died in the Maldives last week have now been found, officials tell the BBC.

item.title: Sen. Bill Cassidy loses primary. And, WHO declares Ebola outbreak a global emergency
item.description: Sen. Bill Cassidy, who voted to convict Trump, lost the Republican primary in Louisiana. And, the WHO has declared a global health emergency over a new Ebola outbreak.

item.title: UK growth forecast upgraded by IMF but risks remain
item.description: Growth has been upgraded from 0.8% to 1% for 2026 in the influential body's latest forecast.

item.title: Why catching insider trading is so tricky nowadays, and just how helpful is it for kids to sleep in?
item.description: Millions of dollars have been made through eerily well-timed bets on prediction markets like Polymarket. We look at why they're so hard to police. And, a new study that supports kids sleeping in.

item.title: At least six Americans exposed to Ebola during DR Congo outbreak
item.description: One of the six Americans believed to have been exposed is experiencing symptoms, according to media reports.

item.title: Pop star Shakira is acquitted in a Spanish tax fraud case
item.description: The decision follows years of tax troubles in Spain for the Colombian superstar. Spanish tax authorities did not prove that the singer was a resident of Spain, the court said in its decision.

item.title: Thousands of U.S. countertop workers could have damaged lungs, safety expert says
item.description: Over 550 men in California have fallen ill after cutting natural or factory-made stone countertops. But epidemiologists say this isn't just a California problem.
